en.title: Graham Farmelo's Authorized Hawking Biography Reveals the Man Behind the Genius
en.summary: The first authorized biography of Stephen Hawking is here, exploring the complex life and groundbreaking work of the beloved physicist. Award-winning biographer Graham Farmelo delves into both Hawking's immense scientific contributions and his deeply personal flaws.
en.body:
The definitive portrait of **Stephen Hawking**, as told by Costa Award-winning biographer **Graham Farmelo**, has finally arrived. Published in September 2026, **Hawking: His Life and Work** marks the first authorized biography of the iconic physicist, promising a comprehensive and accessible journey through his life and groundbreaking scientific ideas. Farmelo, a veteran science writer, navigates the extraordinary intellect and determination of a man who defied his ALS diagnosis to become one of the world's most recognizable figures.

This new biography aims to provide fresh insights, offering readers an in-depth look at Hawking's early life through his rise to global prominence. While acknowledging his monumental achievements in cosmology and theoretical physics, Farmelo also confronts the less comfortable truths about Hawking's personal life. The book reportedly examines his overweening ambition, a tendency to not always acknowledge the contributions of others, and instances of sexism and controlling behavior. These aspects, the book suggests, were often overlooked by both the scientific community and the public, partly due to the immense respect and sympathy garnered by his disability. This comprehensive approach seeks to present a fully rounded picture of the man, moving beyond the universally celebrated image to explore the complexities of his character and impact.

## A Complex Legacy Unveiled

The release of **Hawking: His Life and Work** invites a re-examination of the public perception of **Stephen Hawking**. While his scientific breakthroughs, particularly his work on black holes and the origins of the universe, cemented his legacy, this biography suggests it's time to consider the full spectrum of his personality. Early reviews and the teaser material indicate that Farmelo does not shy away from the darker aspects of Hawking's character, such as alleged bullying and self-aggrandizing behavior. The Guardian's review noted that previous attempts to publish criticisms were met with resistance, with some outlets deeming it "too early" to voice anything other than praise. Farmelo's authorized status, however, suggests a more thorough and perhaps more balanced exploration is now possible, one that can acknowledge his genius while also addressing his personal flaws without diminishing his scientific importance.

## For the Avid Reader and Curious Newcomer

**Graham Farmelo's** meticulous research and engaging narrative style are expected to make **Hawking: His Life and Work** a must-read for both devoted fans of **Stephen Hawking** and newcomers to his story. The biography is designed to be accessible, aiming to demystify complex scientific concepts while illuminating the personal journey of the physicist. For those who have followed Hawking's career, this book offers a chance to understand the man behind the scientific legend more deeply. For those new to his work, it presents an opportunity to engage with a remarkable life story that intertwines profound scientific discovery with significant personal challenges and complexities, all presented with the credibility and enthusiasm WeCult readers expect.

## What's Next

**Hawking: His Life and Work** is now available from **John Murray** in the UK and **Penguin Random House** in the USA. Readers can find the hardcover, paperback, and audiobook editions, offering multiple ways to engage with this definitive biography.

content_raw: A biography of the physicist recognises his achievements, but also reveals the selfish narcissist underneath When I wrote an unadoring review of Stephen Hawking’s final book, a collection of essays published posthumously in 2018, New Scientist suppressed some of my criticisms on the grounds that it was “too early” to voice anything other than praise for the physicist who died, aged 76, that March. It was apparently still too early in 2021, when no British publisher would touch Charles Seife’s exposé of Hawking’s bullying and self-aggrandising behaviour, Hawking Hawking. In this new biography, veteran science writer Graham Farmelo takes a different approach. It is a comprehensive and accessible portrait of a brilliant scientist and an extraordinarily determined man who also possessed deep personal flaws to which the scientific community and the public mostly turned a blind eye. The uncomfortable but unavoidable truth is that Hawking’s overweening ambition and self-promotion, his repeated failure to acknowledge the work of others, his sexism and controlling behaviour were largely ignored because of his disability. I think it is indeed going to take us years to process that. Continue reading...
